title: Very Deep Convolutional Networks for Large-Scale Image Recognition
notes: VGG. Its depth claims are stated on ImageNet, but the underlying comparisons -- deeper is better, 3x3 stacks beat larger filters -- are architectural and can be posed on a small dataset. The absolute ILSVRC results cannot.

claims.text: Increasing the depth of the network from 11 to 19 weight layers reduces classification error.
claims.notes: Reduced form: compare a shallow and a deeper small convnet on a CIFAR-10 subset. The paper notes the benefit saturates, so the direction may be weaker at small scale.

claims.text: A stack of three 3x3 convolution layers outperforms a single 7x7 layer with the same receptive field.
claims.notes: A clean architectural comparison at matched receptive field, cheap to run small.

claims.text: Using 1x1 convolutions to add non-linearity (configuration C) performs worse than using 3x3 convolutions that also capture spatial context (configuration D).
claims.notes: The reported gap is small; three seeds at reduced scale are unlikely to resolve it.

claims.text: Scale jittering during training improves accuracy compared to training at a single fixed scale.
claims.notes: A data augmentation ablation, which transfers to small images.

claims.text: The best VGG configuration reaches 7.3% top-5 test error on ILSVRC-2014.
Local response normalisation does not improve performance over the same network without it.
claims.notes: A claim of no effect. Confirming absence of an effect at reduced scale is inconclusive by construction.

claims.text: An ensemble of two VGG models outperforms either model alone.
claims.notes: Ensembling is a well-established effect that appears at any scale.
